rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate all six peaks while limiting run time. The retention window and critical-pair resolutions will guide adjustments to gradient range, slope, and temperature.
Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient one step to reduce elution time while testing whether the ample resolution margin is preserved.
Shorten the gradient another step while holding composition and temperature constant. The current minimum resolution of 3.47 leaves room to reduce run time while retaining the maximum CRF.
Reduce the gradient duration one more step to seek a faster method with the same maximum CRF. The resolution trend suggests the critical early pair may remain above 1.5 at four minutes.
Test the minimum gradient duration to establish the speed–resolution boundary. The early pair may fall below 1.5; if so, the four-minute gradient remains a fully resolved fallback with maximum CRF.
Back off to the fully resolved four-minute gradient and raise temperature one step to test faster elution. This also measures temperature sensitivity of the critical early pair.

Cooling should improve the early-pair selectivity, based on its deterioration from 40 to 45 C. Combine cooling with a slightly shallower two-minute gradient to seek full resolution faster than the current four-minute method.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step, narrowing the gradient span while retaining the strong endpoint. The shallower slope may lift the early pair above R = 1.5 while the stronger start may shorten late-peak retention.

Shift both gradient endpoints upward while preserving the slope that achieved full resolution in injection 8. This should accelerate the last peak, while testing whether the early pair retains sufficient resolution at the stronger starting composition.
Shift the gradient upward another step at the same slope to accelerate the last peak. Injection 9 preserved the early-pair resolution, so this tests further time savings while targeting CRF 1.000.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step with the endpoint already at its maximum. This may shorten late-peak retention further, while the shallower slope may preserve early-pair resolution despite reduced initial retention.

Raise temperature one step to shorten retention while using the improved early-pair resolution margin from injection 11. This tests whether the two-minute method can remain fully resolved at a higher temperature.

Increase the starting organic fraction one step to seek further time savings at the current temperature. This tests whether narrowing the gradient still benefits the critical early pair as it approaches the dead-time region.

Return to the resolved starting composition and test one temperature step above the fastest fully resolved method. This brackets the thermal resolution limit; injection 12 remains the fallback if the early pair falls below 1.5.

Reduce the gradient span to recover early-pair resolution at 35 C, targeting R above 1.5 through a shallower slope. The strong final composition should still elute all six compounds comfortably within ten minutes.

Lower the starting fraction to retain the early pair beyond the initial solvent window, and return to 30 C to improve selectivity. This targets a fully resolved two-minute method with more resolution margin than injection 12, which remains the fastest maximum-CRF method observed.

Raise the endpoint one step from injection 16 to accelerate the last peak while testing whether the early pair retains full resolution. This refines a neighboring maximum-CRF method without repeating an injection.

Test a slightly shallower gradient adjacent to the fastest maximum-CRF method, injection 12. This should improve the critical-pair resolution margin while keeping all six peaks within a short elution window.

Test whether a lower starting fraction and shallower gradient recover full early-pair resolution at 35 C. Injection 12 remains the fastest maximum-CRF method; this explores a nearby higher-temperature alternative without risking a long elution window.

Return to the cooler, fully resolved region and test a neighboring method expected to provide more early-pair resolution margin than injection 17. The maximum CRF is already secured; injection 12 remains the fastest fully resolved method observed.

Raise the starting fraction one step from injection 20 to shorten late-peak retention while preserving the cooler temperature's selectivity advantage. This tests a nearby fully resolved candidate with potentially more resolution margin than the fastest method, injection 12.

Test whether cooling to 25 C restores early-pair resolution at the stronger starting composition that failed at 30 C. This checks the remaining nearby high-organic boundary; injection 12 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Use the final injection to test a nearby two-minute method expected to retain maximum CRF with additional early-pair resolution margin. Injection 12 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, with the last peak at 2.58 minutes.
